title: 2027 Cricket World Cup Set for October Start Across Southern Africa
excerpt: The ICC has penciled in a 14-team, 54-match tournament from October 4 to November 21 across South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, reviving the Super Six format for the first time since 2003.
body:
• The 2027 ODI World Cup runs October 4 to November 21 across South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, marking cricket's return to Africa after 24 years
  • The tournament expands to 14 teams and revives the Super Six format last used in 2003, with 54 total matches planned
  • South Africa will host at least 41 matches across eight venues, while Zimbabwe gets 8-10 games including at a new Victoria Falls stadium
  • India is expected to be drawn alongside Pakistan and South Africa in one of two seven-team groups

Cricket Returns to Africa

Cricket's showpiece event is heading back to the African continent for the first time in nearly a quarter century. The ICC has provisionally scheduled the 2027 ODI World Cup to run from October 4 to November 21 across South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, according to ESPNcricinfo.

"The region also holds deep historical significance as the place where Mahatma Gandhi began his activism — and the October 4 start date falls just two days after Gandhi Jayanti."

The dates were agreed upon at the ICC Board Meeting in Ahmedabad in May, with final confirmation expected at the ICC Annual General Meeting in Edinburgh. The tournament will feature 54 matches — up from 48 in the 2023 edition hosted by India — and mark the first time Namibia has hosted World Cup cricket.

The last time the World Cup visited Africa was in 2003, when Australia defeated India in the final at Johannesburg's Wanderers Stadium. That tournament remains etched in the memories of Indian cricket fans for Sachin Tendulkar's iconic innings against Pakistan at Centurion and India's march to the final.

A Bigger, Bolder Format

After two consecutive editions with just 10 teams competing in a round-robin format, the 2027 World Cup expands to 14 teams and brings back the Super Six stage last used in 2003.

The 14 teams will be divided into two groups of seven. Each team plays six group-stage matches, with the top three from each group advancing to the Super Six round. Cross-group matches then determine the four semifinalists. Eight teams qualify automatically based on ICC rankings, while six more will earn their places through qualifying tournaments.

Venues Across Three Nations

South Africa will shoulder the bulk of hosting duties, staging at least 41 of the 54 matches across eight venues: Centurion, Johannesburg, Bloemfontein, Durban, East London, Gqeberha, Paarl and Cape Town. Zimbabwe will host between eight and 10 matches at Harare Sports Club, Queens in Bulawayo and the new Fale Mosi-oa-Tunya International Cricket Stadium in Victoria Falls, which is being completed later this year. Namibia will stage three matches.

It will be South Africa's first ICC men's event since the 2009 Champions Trophy. The country also hosted the inaugural 2007 T20 World Cup — the tournament MS Dhoni's India famously won — as well as the 2023 Women's T20 World Cup.

What It Means for India

India is among the eight teams expected to qualify directly. Early reports indicate the team could be drawn in the same group as Pakistan, South Africa, Sri Lanka, Afghanistan, Zimbabwe and a qualifier, though groups have not been officially confirmed by the ICC.

For the Indian diaspora, particularly the sizable communities in Southern Africa, the tournament offers a rare chance to watch India play on the continent. South Africa is home to one of the oldest Indian diaspora communities in the world, with roots stretching back to the 1860s. The region also holds deep historical significance as the place where Mahatma Gandhi began his activism — and the October 4 start date falls just two days after Gandhi Jayanti.

What Comes Next

The ICC is expected to release the full match schedule following its Annual General Meeting. Qualifying tournaments will determine the remaining six spots in the 14-team field, with South Africa and Zimbabwe slotting in automatically as Full Members. Namibia, however, must earn their place through the qualification process. For defending champions Australia and a resurgent India, the 2027 edition opens the new 2027-2031 Future Tours Program cycle.
